drinks.name: London Fog
drinks.intro: A fragrant tea latte that blends Earl Grey, steamed milk, and a touch of sweetness.
drinks.about: The London Fog gets its distinctive flavor from bergamot-scented Earl Grey tea. Steamed milk and vanilla create a soft, creamy drink that balances the tea's citrusy aroma.
drinks.funFact: Despite the name, the London Fog was most likely born in a Vancouver café in the 1990s. Nobody’s sure who named it, but most people guess it’s the way steamed milk clouds the tea.

hot.label: Hot
method: Steep the tea bag in hot water for 3–5 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla syrup.
Steam the milk until soft and frothy.
Pour the milk into the tea and serve.

iced.label: Iced
method: Steep the tea bags in hot water for 5 minutes for a strong brew.
Stir in the vanilla syrup and let it cool.
Pour over a glass of ice.
Top with cold milk and stir.

stories.note: Just relaxing and enjoying the day. Get it with vanilla or lavender.

stories.moment: On the way to an early morning class
stories.note: The only thing that gets me through 8:30 lectures.

drinks.name: Mimosa
drinks.intro: A bright, bubbly brunch classic made for slow mornings and celebratory afternoons.
drinks.about: The mimosa combines sparkling wine with orange juice for a drink that is crisp, citrusy, and lightly sweet. Its simplicity makes it easy to adapt with different juices and sparkling wines.
drinks.funFact: The cocktail is traditionally associated with the Hôtel Ritz Paris, where it became popular in the 1920s.

classic.label: Classic
method: Fill a champagne flute halfway with chilled orange juice.
Top with chilled champagne or sparkling wine.
Gently stir and serve immediately.

zero-proof.label: Zero-proof

ingredients.item: Sparkling water or non-alcoholic sparkling wine

method: Fill a champagne flute halfway with chilled orange juice.
Top with sparkling water or non-alcoholic sparkling wine.
Gently stir and serve immediately.

drinks.name: Matcha
drinks.intro: A vibrant green tea drink with a rich, earthy flavor and a long history rooted in Japanese tea culture.
drinks.about: Matcha is made by whisking finely ground green tea powder with water, creating a smooth, slightly bitter drink with a naturally creamy texture. It can also be combined with milk and sweetener to make a matcha latte.
drinks.funFact: Instead of steeping the leaves and throwing them away, matcha is the leaf itself, ground into powder. That’s also why it has more caffeine than regular green tea.

hot.label: Hot
method: Sift the matcha powder into a bowl.
Add the hot water, about 175°F / 80°C (not boiling).
Whisk vigorously until smooth and frothy. No bamboo whisk? Shake the matcha and water in a sealed jar.
Steam the milk and pour it in for a latte.

iced.label: Iced
method: Sift the matcha powder into a bowl.
Add the hot water, about 175°F / 80°C (not boiling).
Whisk vigorously until smooth and frothy. No bamboo whisk? Shake the matcha and water in a sealed jar.
Fill a glass with ice and cold milk, then pour the matcha over.

drinks.name: Margarita
drinks.intro: A bright combination of tequila, citrus, and salt that balances sweet, sour, and savory flavors.
drinks.about: A classic Margarita combines tequila with lime juice and orange liqueur. It is shaken with ice and served either over fresh ice or strained into a chilled glass, often with a salted rim.
drinks.funFact: The frozen margarita machine was invented in 1971 by a Dallas restaurant owner who rigged up a soft-serve ice cream machine. The original now lives in the Smithsonian.

classic.label: Classic
method: Rim a glass with lime and dip in salt.
Shake tequila, lime juice, and orange liqueur with ice.
Strain over fresh ice.
Garnish with a lime wedge.

zero-proof.label: Zero-proof
method: Rim a glass with lime and dip in salt.
Shake lime juice, orange juice, and agave with ice.
Strain over fresh ice and top with soda water.
Garnish with a lime wedge.

drinks.name: Cosmopolitan
drinks.intro: A sharply pink cocktail with a citrusy personality and unmistakable late-night energy.
drinks.about: The Cosmopolitan combines vodka, cranberry juice, orange liqueur, and lime juice. It is tart, lightly sweet, and usually served chilled in a martini glass.
drinks.funFact: The Cosmopolitan became particularly famous in the late 1990s and early 2000s after appearing frequently on Sex and the City.

classic.label: Classic
method: Add vodka, cranberry juice, triple sec, and lime juice to a shaker.
Add ice and shake vigorously.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an orange twist.

zero-proof.label: Zero-proof
method: Shake cranberry juice, lime juice, orange juice, and simple syrup with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Top with a splash of soda.
Garnish with an orange twist.

drinks.name: Shirley Temple
drinks.intro: A sweet, sparkling mocktail that has been a fixture of restaurant menus for generations.
drinks.about: The classic Shirley Temple combines ginger ale or lemon-lime soda with grenadine and is usually finished with a maraschino cherry. It is sweet, fizzy, and completely alcohol-free.
drinks.funFact: The drink was named after child movie star Shirley Temple, although she reportedly disliked the drink herself.

classic.label: Classic
method: Fill a glass with ice.
Add the ginger ale or lemon-lime soda.
Add the grenadine.
Stir gently and garnish with a maraschino cherry.

dirty.label: Dirty Shirley
method: Fill a glass with ice.
Add the vodka, then the ginger ale or lemon-lime soda.
Add the grenadine.
Stir gently and garnish with a maraschino cherry.
